title: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer (PCSE) practice questions

exams.name: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A company wants users and groups from its on-premises Active Directory synchronized to Cloud Identity on a schedule. What should it use?
options: Cloud Scheduler with a script that emails users
questions.correct_rationale: GCDS synchronizes users and groups from LDAP or Active Directory to Cloud Identity or Google Workspace.
questions.distractor_summary: Storage Transfer moves objects, email scripts do not sync identities, and IAP controls application access.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Employees must sign in to Google Cloud with their existing corporate identity provider credentials. What should be configured?
options: A separate Google password for each employee
Service account keys for each user
SAML-based single sign-on between Cloud Identity and the corporate IdP
questions.correct_rationale: SSO lets Cloud Identity delegate authentication to the external IdP.
questions.distractor_summary: Separate passwords add risk, service account keys are for workloads, and VPC Service Controls protect data perimeters.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is a super administrator account in Cloud Identity?
options: A service account used by Compute Engine
A role for viewing billing only
An account with full control over the Cloud Identity or Workspace account, which should be protected and used sparingly
A default account for every user
questions.correct_rationale: Super admins can manage everything, including other admins, so they need strong protection.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a service account, billing-only role, or default user state.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Super administrator accounts must be protected against phishing. What is the strongest recommendation?
options: Share one super admin password among the IT team
Enforce 2-Step Verification with security keys for super admins and keep a small number of dedicated accounts
Disable 2-Step Verification for admins to avoid lockouts
questions.correct_rationale: Security keys resist phishing, and limiting accounts reduces exposure.
questions.distractor_summary: Shared passwords, SMS codes, and disabled 2SV are weaker.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Which tool lets an organization see and manage which external identity provider each user signs in with, using different profiles for different groups?
options: SSO profiles assigned to organizational units or groups in the Admin console
questions.correct_rationale: SSO profiles can be assigned per OU or group.
questions.distractor_summary: Asset Inventory, Monitoring, and Artifact Registry do not manage sign-in.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: When an employee leaves, their access to Google Cloud must be removed quickly and consistently. What is the best practice?
options: Manage access through groups and suspend or delete the user in Cloud Identity, ideally driven by the HR or IdP lifecycle
Remove the user from every project's IAM policy by hand
Delete the user's Cloud Storage buckets
questions.correct_rationale: Central identity lifecycle management removes access everywhere at once.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual removal misses projects, and key rotation or bucket deletion do not address the user.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is the purpose of organizational units in the Cloud Identity Admin console?
options: Applying different user settings and policies, such as 2-Step Verification enforcement, to groups of users
questions.correct_rationale: OUs organize users for policy settings.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not organize VMs, subnets, or storage rules.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Users are being provisioned automatically from Microsoft Entra ID to Cloud Identity. Which protocol is commonly used for user provisioning?
options: SCIM through the Google Cloud or Workspace gallery app in Entra ID
questions.correct_rationale: SCIM automates user provisioning between identity systems.
questions.distractor_summary: SMTP, SNMP, and FTP are not provisioning protocols.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What does Workforce Identity Federation allow?
options: Running workloads on premises without credentials
Letting users from an external IdP access Google Cloud resources without syncing them to Cloud Identity
questions.correct_rationale: Workforce Identity Federation maps external identities to IAM principals.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not run workloads, encrypt data, or create firewall rules.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A company wants context-aware sign-in rules, such as blocking access from unmanaged devices. What should be used?
options: Context-Aware Access with Access Context Manager access levels
questions.correct_rationale: Context-Aware Access uses device and location attributes in access decisions.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT, CDN, and Scheduler do not evaluate sign-in context.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: An application on Compute Engine must call Cloud Storage APIs. What is the recommended way to authenticate?
options: Attach a user-managed service account with only the needed roles to the VM
Download a service account key and store it on the VM disk
Use the default Compute Engine service account with the Editor role
questions.correct_rationale: Attached service accounts provide credentials through the metadata server without keys.
questions.distractor_summary: Keys on disk can leak, personal credentials break separation, and default accounts often have excessive roles.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Which organization policy constraint prevents creation of service account keys?
questions.correct_rationale: This constraint blocks new service account keys.
questions.distractor_summary: The others restrict external IPs, bucket access mode, and locations.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A CI system running outside Google Cloud must deploy to Google Cloud without long-lived keys. What should be used?
options: A service account key stored in the CI secrets
Workload Identity Federation with the CI system's OIDC tokens, impersonating a service account
questions.correct_rationale: Federation exchanges external tokens for short-lived Google credentials.
questions.distractor_summary: Stored keys are long-lived, user tokens break separation, and public access is unsafe.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What does the Service Account Token Creator role allow?
options: Impersonating a service account to create short-lived credentials for it
questions.correct_rationale: Token Creator lets a principal generate tokens as the service account.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not create projects, delete buckets, or manage billing.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Developers sometimes need to act as a deployment service account for testing. What is the safest approach?
options: Email them the service account key
Grant them permission to impersonate the service account and use short-lived tokens, with audit logging
questions.correct_rationale: Impersonation avoids keys and is logged.
questions.distractor_summary: Emailing keys, broad Owner rights, and shared CI credentials are risky.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Why is using the default Compute Engine service account discouraged?
options: It is often granted the broad Editor role automatically, which violates least privilege
It is deleted after one day
It only works in one zone
questions.correct_rationale: Default accounts may carry broad permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: It can call APIs, is not deleted daily, and is not zonal.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Service account keys already exist in a project and must be found and reduced. What should be used?
options: Recommender and Policy Intelligence insights for unused keys and accounts, plus Cloud Asset Inventory to list keys
questions.correct_rationale: Insights and inventory show where keys exist and which are unused.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN, NAT, and Artifact Registry do not report on keys.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: How does GKE Workload Identity Federation help pods access Google Cloud APIs?
options: It gives every pod the node's credentials with full access
It disables API access for pods
It lets Kubernetes service accounts act as IAM principals, so pods get credentials without keys
questions.correct_rationale: Workload Identity maps Kubernetes identities to IAM securely.
questions.distractor_summary: Node credentials are too broad, ConfigMaps are not for keys, and API access is not disabled.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A service account is no longer used, but the team is not sure. What is a safe first step?
options: Disable the service account, monitor for errors, and delete it later if nothing breaks
questions.correct_rationale: Disabling is reversible, unlike deletion.
questions.distractor_summary: Immediate deletion can break workloads, Owner adds risk, and new keys add exposure.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is a service agent in Google Cloud?
options: A Google-managed service account that a Google Cloud service uses to access resources on your behalf
questions.correct_rationale: Service agents let services such as Cloud Build act in your project.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a person, key file, or network.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Users must use 2-Step Verification for Google Cloud access. Where is this enforced?
options: In the Admin console security settings for Cloud Identity or Workspace, applied to the right OUs
questions.correct_rationale: 2SV is enforced at the identity layer.
questions.distractor_summary: Firewalls, bucket policies, and DNS do not enforce sign-in methods.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is the session length setting for Google Cloud used for?
options: Controlling how often users must reauthenticate for console and gcloud access
Setting the Cloud SQL connection timeout
questions.correct_rationale: Session controls require periodic reauthentication.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not affect SQL timeouts, VMs, or object age.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: An application must authenticate users of a web app with Google sign-in and other providers, with minimal custom code. What should be used?
options: Service account keys for each user
questions.correct_rationale: Identity Platform provides customer identity and access management for apps.
questions.distractor_summary: Admin accounts, service account keys, and VPC SC are not app user auth.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is the purpose of OAuth 2.0 scopes when a user grants an app access to Google APIs?
options: Limiting which resources and actions the app's token can access
questions.correct_rationale: Scopes restrict the access granted to the app.
questions.distractor_summary: Scopes are unrelated to encryption, machines, or subnets.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A company wants to block third-party apps from accessing users' Google data unless approved. What should be configured?
options: App access control in the Admin console to restrict OAuth app access to trusted apps
questions.correct_rationale: API controls manage which apps can access user data.
questions.distractor_summary: Armor, NAT, and location policies do not control OAuth apps.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Which credential type should never be committed to source code?
options: Service account keys and API keys
questions.correct_rationale: Keys grant access and must be kept secret.
questions.distractor_summary: Project IDs, regions, and doc URLs are not secrets.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: API keys are used by a web front end. How can their misuse be limited?
options: Apply API restrictions to specific APIs and application restrictions such as HTTP referrers or IP addresses
Share the key publicly with documentation
Use the same key for every project
questions.correct_rationale: Key restrictions limit where and for which APIs a key works.
questions.distractor_summary: Unrestricted and shared keys can be abused.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What does reauthentication for sensitive actions, sometimes called step-up, achieve?
options: Requires users to verify again before high-risk operations, lowering the impact of stolen sessions
questions.correct_rationale: Step-up checks reduce risk from hijacked sessions.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not lengthen sessions, remove MFA, or grant roles.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Engineers need SSH access to Linux VMs tied to their Google identities, with 2SV, and no SSH key management. What should be used?
options: Serial console with a shared password
questions.correct_rationale: OS Login ties SSH access to IAM and Cloud Identity.
questions.distractor_summary: Metadata keys need manual management, and shared passwords are insecure.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What are short-lived credentials in Google Cloud?
options: OAuth access tokens or ID tokens generated for a service account that expire quickly, often after one hour
questions.correct_rationale: Short-lived tokens limit damage if leaked.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not permanent keys, stored passwords, or public certificates.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A team needs permissions to manage Compute Engine instances in one project, but nothing else. What should be granted?
options: The basic Editor role on the organization
A predefined role such as Compute Instance Admin (v1) on that project, to a group
The Owner role on the project
The Viewer role on the folder
questions.correct_rationale: Predefined roles at the right scope follow least privilege.
questions.distractor_summary: Editor and Owner are too broad, and Viewer cannot manage instances.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is a custom IAM role?
options: A role with a hand-picked list of permissions created at the organization or project level
A role created automatically for each user
questions.correct_rationale: Custom roles fit needs not met by predefined roles.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not automatic, a firewall rule, or a budget.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Nobody except a security group should be able to delete Cloud KMS keys, even project Owners. What can enforce this?
options: An IAM deny policy that denies key destruction permissions for all principals except the security group
A custom role for the security group only
questions.correct_rationale: Deny policies override allow policies, so they block Owners too.
questions.distractor_summary: Custom roles only grant, Armor protects apps, and billing alerts do not restrict actions.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What do IAM Conditions allow?
options: Granting roles only when conditions are met, such as a time window or resource name prefix
questions.correct_rationale: Conditions add attribute-based limits to role bindings.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not encrypt, create networks, or alert.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Access to a project must be granted for only eight hours for an emergency. What is a good approach?
options: Grant Owner permanently and remember to remove it
Use a time-bound IAM condition or Privileged Access Manager grant with approval
Disable audit logs during the emergency
questions.correct_rationale: Time-bound grants expire automatically.
questions.distractor_summary: Permanent grants linger, shared accounts lack accountability, and disabling logs hides activity.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is Privileged Access Manager (PAM) in Google Cloud?
options: A service for just-in-time, temporary elevation of IAM roles with justification and approval
questions.correct_rationale: PAM provides temporary, approved access to privileged roles.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a firewall, key service, or log sink.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Users report they cannot access a bucket even though they have Storage Object Viewer on the project. What should be checked?
options: Deny policies, IAM conditions, VPC Service Controls perimeters, and organization policies that could block access
The number of objects in the bucket
questions.correct_rationale: Several controls can block access beyond allow policies.
questions.distractor_summary: Storage class, object count, and CDN do not usually cause access denial.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Which tool explains why a principal has or does not have a specific permission on a resource?
questions.correct_rationale: Policy Troubleshooter evaluates IAM and related policies for a request.
questions.distractor_summary: Trace, Profiler, and Build do not analyze access.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A security team wants to find roles granted to users that they have not used in 90 days. What should they use?
questions.correct_rationale: Role recommendations suggest removing unused permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: Uptime checks, DNS, and NAT logs do not analyze IAM usage.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Why should basic roles such as Owner, Editor, and Viewer be avoided in production?
options: They do not work in production projects
They grant broad permissions across many services, which breaks least privilege
questions.correct_rationale: Basic roles are too broad for most needs.
questions.distractor_summary: They still work and exist, and they are not billing-only.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A company wants separate controls for production and development, inherited by all projects in each. What should be designed?
options: Folders for production and development under the organization, with IAM and org policies applied at folder level
questions.correct_rationale: Folders group projects and pass down policies.
questions.distractor_summary: One project mixes environments, many orgs are hard to govern, and labels do not enforce policies.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: How are IAM policies inherited in the Google Cloud resource hierarchy?
options: Lower levels override and remove higher-level grants
Policies set at a higher level, such as a folder, are inherited by projects and resources below, and allow policies are additive
questions.correct_rationale: Allow policies are combined down the hierarchy.
questions.distractor_summary: Lower levels cannot remove inherited grants (deny policies are different), and inheritance does exist.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Resources must be created only in EU regions across the organization. What should be configured?
options: The gcp.resourceLocations organization policy constraint, set to EU locations at the organization
questions.correct_rationale: The resource locations constraint restricts where resources can be created.
questions.distractor_summary: Firewalls, Armor, and roles do not limit locations.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What is the purpose of organization policy constraints?
options: Setting guardrails on how resources can be configured, such as blocking external IPs or public buckets
questions.correct_rationale: Org policies restrict configurations regardless of IAM permissions.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not grant permissions, encrypt, or monitor.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Public access to Cloud Storage buckets must be blocked across all projects. What should be enforced?
questions.correct_rationale: Public access prevention blocks public ACLs and IAM grants on buckets.
questions.distractor_summary: Lifecycle rules, CDN, and firewalls do not stop public grants.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What happens to org policies when a project is moved to another folder?
options: The project keeps the old folder's policies forever
The project inherits the policies of its new parent folder
The project is copied, not moved
questions.correct_rationale: Inherited policies follow the current parent.
questions.distractor_summary: Old inheritance does not persist, policies are not deleted, and projects are moved.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: A team wants to test a new org policy before enforcing it. What should they use?
options: A dry-run organization policy and Policy Simulator to see the impact
Apply it to the organization with no testing
Only discuss it in a meeting
questions.correct_rationale: Dry-run and simulation show violations without blocking.
questions.distractor_summary: Immediate enforcement risks outages, and discussion does not test impact.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Which Google Cloud service provides a blueprint-based landing zone with recommended security settings?
options: The enterprise foundations blueprint, often deployed with Terraform
questions.correct_rationale: The foundations blueprint sets up a secure organization structure.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN, Functions, and Memorystore are workload services.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: Projects must be created only by a central team. What should be configured?
options: Grant the Project Creator role only to that team, removing it from the organization's default domain grant
questions.correct_rationale: Restricting Project Creator controls who can create projects.
questions.distractor_summary: Owner for all is unsafe, and NAT and labels do not control project creation.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.domain: 1. Configuring access within a cloud solution environment
questions.question: What are tags in Google Cloud used for in security?
options: Text labels only for billing reports
Key-value resources that can be bound to resources and used in IAM conditions and firewall policies
questions.correct_rationale: Tags support conditional access and network policies.
questions.distractor_summary: Labels are for billing and organization, and tags are not keys or routes.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A public web application on a global external Application Load Balancer must be protected from SQL injection and from traffic coming from certain countries. What should be used?
options: Google Cloud Armor security policies with preconfigured WAF rules and geo-based rules
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Armor provides WAF and geo filtering at the load balancer.
questions.distractor_summary: VPC firewalls work at layer 3 and 4 inside the VPC, NAT handles outbound, and Private Google Access reaches Google APIs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Which Cloud Armor feature limits the number of requests from a client in a time window?
options: Rate limiting rules (throttle or rate-based ban)
questions.correct_rationale: Rate limiting rules throttle or ban clients that exceed thresholds.
questions.distractor_summary: XSS rules match attacks, IP lists match sources, and Adaptive Protection detects anomalies.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A company wants machine learning to detect layer 7 DDoS attacks against its backend services and suggest rules. What should be enabled?
questions.correct_rationale: Adaptive Protection models normal traffic and alerts on anomalies with suggested rules.
questions.distractor_summary: DNSSEC protects DNS, Flow Logs record traffic, and NAT logs show translations.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What does Identity-Aware Proxy (IAP) provide?
options: Access control to applications and VMs based on user identity and context, without a VPN
questions.correct_rationale: IAP verifies identity before allowing access to protected resources.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not manage keys, scan data, or host DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Administrators need SSH to VMs with no external IPs and without a bastion host. What should be used?
options: Assign public IPs to all VMs
IAP TCP forwarding, with firewall rules allowing the IAP range 35.235.240.0/20
questions.correct_rationale: IAP TCP forwarding tunnels SSH through Google with IAM checks.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IPs and open ports expose VMs, and CDN is for content.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What is a hierarchical firewall policy?
options: A firewall rule for one VM only
A Cloud Armor rule for load balancers
A firewall policy applied at the organization or folder level that is evaluated before VPC firewall rules
questions.correct_rationale: Hierarchical policies let central teams enforce rules across projects.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not per-VM, Cloud Armor, or routes.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A central security team must block traffic to a known malicious IP range for all VPCs in the organization, and project teams must not override it. What should be configured?
options: VPC firewall rules in each project
A Cloud Armor policy on each VM
A hierarchical firewall policy at the organization with a deny rule and no goto_next for that range
questions.correct_rationale: Organization-level deny rules apply before project rules and cannot be overridden by them.
questions.distractor_summary: Per-project rules can be changed, Armor protects load balancers, and DNS policies do not block IPs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Which Cloud Next Generation Firewall (NGFW) tier adds intrusion prevention with threat signatures?
options: Cloud NGFW Standard only for FQDNs
questions.correct_rationale: The Enterprise tier provides intrusion prevention through firewall endpoints.
questions.distractor_summary: Essentials and Standard provide basic and FQDN features, and the default firewall has no IPS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Egress from VMs must be allowed only to specific domains. Which Cloud NGFW feature fits?
options: FQDN objects in firewall policy rules (Cloud NGFW Standard)
questions.correct_rationale: FQDN objects let egress rules target domain names.
questions.distractor_summary: Tags identify targets, NAT translates addresses, and Private Google Access reaches Google APIs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What is the effect of the implied rules in a VPC network?
options: Implied rules deny all ingress and allow all egress unless other rules override them
questions.correct_rationale: Every VPC has implied deny ingress and allow egress rules at the lowest priority.
questions.distractor_summary: The other descriptions are wrong.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A web app behind an external Application Load Balancer must also reject requests that do not come through the load balancer. What should be done?
options: Give backends external IPs and allow all traffic
Use Cloud NAT for inbound traffic
Allow ingress to backends only from Google Front End ranges such as 130.211.0.0/22 and 35.191.0.0/16, and keep backends without external IPs
questions.correct_rationale: Backends should only accept proxy and health check traffic from Google ranges.
questions.distractor_summary: External IPs expose backends, NAT is outbound, and health checks need those ranges.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Which Cloud Armor feature lets you block or allow traffic based on reputation lists maintained by Google?
options: Custom rules with fixed IPs only
questions.correct_rationale: Threat intelligence provides curated lists such as known malicious IPs.
questions.distractor_summary: Custom fixed IPs need manual updates, and DNS logs and Flow Logs do not enforce rules.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Bots are abusing a login page. What Cloud Armor feature can help separate humans from bots?
options: reCAPTCHA integration with Cloud Armor bot management
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Armor can use reCAPTCHA assessments in rules.
questions.distractor_summary: VM size, Private Google Access, and lifecycle rules do not stop bots.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What is the purpose of a Cloud Armor preview mode on a rule?
options: Logging what the rule would do without enforcing it, to test for false positives
questions.correct_rationale: Preview mode helps tune rules safely.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not make rules permanent, disable logs, or encrypt.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Development and production workloads must be network-isolated but share common services. What design fits?
options: Separate VPCs or Shared VPC host projects per environment, with controlled connectivity to a shared services VPC
One VPC with all workloads and no firewall rules
questions.correct_rationale: Separate networks per environment with controlled links provide isolation.
questions.distractor_summary: A flat network, public IPs, and one subnet do not isolate environments.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What is Shared VPC?
options: A model where a host project owns a VPC network and service projects use its subnets
questions.correct_rationale: Shared VPC centralizes network control while teams manage their own projects.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a VPN, IP pool, or load balancer.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Service project teams in a Shared VPC must only deploy into their own subnets. What should be granted?
options: Compute Network Admin on the host project
The Compute Network User role on specific subnets, not on the whole host project
questions.correct_rationale: Subnet-level Network User limits where teams can deploy.
questions.distractor_summary: Network Admin and Owner are too broad, and Viewer cannot deploy.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Which statement about VPC Network Peering is correct?
options: Peering is transitive across any number of networks
Peering is not transitive, and peered networks cannot have overlapping subnet ranges
questions.correct_rationale: Peering connects two networks privately without transitivity.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not transitive, needs no public IPs, and stays on Google's network.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Firewall rules should apply only to VMs running a specific application, regardless of IP. What is the most secure targeting method?
options: Target all instances in the network
Target by service account in firewall rules or use secure tags in firewall policies
Use network tags anyone with instance edit rights can change
questions.correct_rationale: Service accounts and secure tags are controlled by IAM, unlike network tags.
questions.distractor_summary: All-instance rules are too broad, IPs change, and network tags are easier to tamper with.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What is the priority range of VPC firewall rules?
options: 0 to 65535, where lower numbers have higher priority
questions.correct_rationale: Lower priority numbers are evaluated first.
questions.distractor_summary: The other ranges or orderings are wrong.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A network virtual appliance must inspect all traffic between two VPCs. What design fits?
options: A multi-NIC appliance VM with interfaces in each VPC and custom routes sending traffic through it
questions.correct_rationale: Multi-NIC appliances and routes put inspection between networks.
questions.distractor_summary: Peering bypasses the appliance, and NAT or Private Google Access do not inspect.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What is the purpose of Packet Mirroring in Google Cloud?
options: Cloning traffic from VMs to collectors for inspection by intrusion detection tools
questions.correct_rationale: Packet Mirroring sends copies of traffic to analysis tools.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not encrypt, balance, or block.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Microservices in GKE must only talk to the services they need. What should be configured?
options: A single firewall rule allowing all pods
Kubernetes network policies (with GKE Dataplane V2) restricting pod traffic
questions.correct_rationale: Network policies control pod-to-pod traffic.
questions.distractor_summary: Allow-all rules, public IPs, and CDN do not segment services.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What does VPC Service Controls protect against?
options: Data exfiltration from Google-managed services by creating service perimeters around projects
questions.correct_rationale: Service perimeters restrict API access to resources from outside the perimeter.
questions.distractor_summary: DDoS, injection, and passwords are handled by other controls.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A BigQuery dataset in a perimeter must be read by a partner's project outside the perimeter. How should this be allowed?
options: Create an ingress rule (or a perimeter bridge where appropriate) that allows the specific identity and project to call BigQuery
questions.correct_rationale: Ingress and egress rules allow narrow exceptions to perimeters.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing the perimeter or making data public defeats the protection, and logging changes nothing.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What does the dry-run mode of a VPC Service Controls perimeter do?
options: Logs requests that would be denied without blocking them
questions.correct_rationale: Dry-run lets you test perimeters safely.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not block, delete, or encrypt.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Users from the corporate network should reach protected APIs inside a perimeter, but others should not. What should be used?
options: A firewall rule on a VM
An access level in Access Context Manager based on corporate IP ranges or device policy, added to the perimeter
questions.correct_rationale: Access levels let trusted contexts reach perimeter resources.
questions.distractor_summary: Public datasets, VM firewalls, and NAT do not apply to API perimeters.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: VMs without external IPs must reach Cloud Storage and BigQuery APIs. What should be enabled?
options: Private Google Access on the subnet
questions.correct_rationale: Private Google Access lets internal VMs reach Google APIs.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN, external IPs, and Armor are not needed for this.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What does Private Service Connect provide?
options: Private endpoints in your VPC to reach Google APIs, managed services, or services published by other organizations
questions.correct_rationale: Private Service Connect exposes services through internal IP endpoints.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not a public load balancer, registrar, or KMS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: On-premises systems must access Google APIs privately over Cloud Interconnect, and requests must stay within a VPC Service Controls perimeter. What should be configured?
options: Use the restricted.googleapis.com VIP or a Private Service Connect endpoint for APIs, with DNS on premises pointing to it and routes advertised over Interconnect
Use the public googleapis.com endpoints over the internet
Use Cloud NAT for on-premises traffic
questions.correct_rationale: The restricted VIP or PSC endpoints keep API traffic private and compatible with perimeters.
questions.distractor_summary: Public endpoints cross the internet, NAT and CDN do not provide private API access.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What does Cloud NAT do?
options: Lets VMs without external IPs make outbound connections to the internet, with no inbound connections allowed
Allows inbound internet traffic to private VMs
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud NAT provides managed outbound translation.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not allow inbound, encrypt, or resolve DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A company needs a private, high-bandwidth connection between its data center and Google Cloud. What fits?
questions.correct_rationale: Interconnect provides private physical connectivity.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN, the open internet, and Private Google Access do not connect data centers.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Which service provides encrypted IPsec connectivity over the internet between on premises and a VPC?
questions.correct_rationale: HA VPN creates IPsec tunnels with a 99.99 percent SLA when configured correctly.
questions.distractor_summary: Interconnect is not encrypted by default, and Armor and DNS do not create tunnels.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Traffic over Dedicated Interconnect must be encrypted. What options exist?
options: HA VPN over Cloud Interconnect, or MACsec for Cloud Interconnect
questions.correct_rationale: HA VPN over Interconnect and MACsec add encryption to the private link.
questions.distractor_summary: Interconnect does not encrypt by default, and NAT and Private Google Access do not encrypt.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What is the purpose of private services access?
options: Connecting your VPC privately to Google-managed services such as Cloud SQL through a peering with a service producer network
questions.correct_rationale: Private services access gives managed services internal IPs.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not make services public, host DNS, or create firewall rules.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: DNS queries for private zones must resolve from on premises over the VPN. What should be configured?
options: A Cloud DNS inbound server policy, with on-premises DNS forwarding to the inbound forwarder addresses
questions.correct_rationale: Inbound server policies let on-premises resolvers query Cloud DNS.
questions.distractor_summary: Public zones expose records, and Armor and CDN do not handle DNS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: What does a Cloud DNS response policy allow?
options: Overriding DNS answers for specific names within a VPC, for example to block domains or redirect APIs
questions.correct_rationale: Response policies change answers for matching names.
questions.distractor_summary: They do not register domains, encrypt, or balance loads.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A producer team wants to offer an internal service to consumers in other VPCs and organizations without peering. What should they publish?
options: A public IP on each backend
A VPC peering to each consumer
A Private Service Connect service attachment behind an internal load balancer
questions.correct_rationale: Service attachments let consumers connect through PSC endpoints without peering.
questions.distractor_summary: Public IPs expose the service, peering does not scale and requires non-overlapping ranges, and NAT is outbound.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: Which load balancers can Cloud Armor security policies be attached to?
options: Supported Application Load Balancers and some proxy and passthrough Network Load Balancers, through backend services
questions.correct_rationale: Cloud Armor policies attach to backend services of supported load balancers.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT, VPN, and DNS are not Cloud Armor targets.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.question: A VPC Service Controls perimeter blocks a Cloud Function from writing to a bucket in another project inside a different perimeter. What fits?
options: An egress rule from the first perimeter and an ingress rule in the second, scoped to the identity and service
questions.correct_rationale: Paired egress and ingress rules allow specific cross-perimeter access.
questions.distractor_summary: Removing perimeters or public buckets weaken protection, and logging is unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: A company must find credit card numbers and national ID numbers stored in Cloud Storage and BigQuery. What should be used?
options: Sensitive Data Protection discovery and inspection with built-in infoTypes
questions.correct_rationale: Sensitive Data Protection scans data for sensitive infoTypes.
questions.distractor_summary: CDN, Flow Logs, and Scheduler do not inspect content.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: What does de-identification in Sensitive Data Protection do?
options: Transforms sensitive values, for example by masking, tokenizing, or bucketing, so data can be used with less risk
questions.correct_rationale: De-identification reduces exposure while keeping data useful.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not delete data, encrypt disks, or block traffic.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: Analysts must join datasets on customer IDs without seeing the real IDs, and authorized staff must be able to reverse the change. What technique fits?

questions.correct_rationale: Deterministic tokenization keeps joins possible and allows re-identification with the key.
questions.distractor_summary: Redaction and masking lose the values, and bucketing changes values irreversibly.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: What is a custom infoType in Sensitive Data Protection?
options: A predefined detector for email addresses
A user-defined detector, such as a regex or dictionary, for organization-specific sensitive data
questions.correct_rationale: Custom infoTypes find data like internal employee IDs.
questions.distractor_summary: Predefined detectors are built in, and firewall rules and key rings are unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: Sensitive data findings must be visible to the security team centrally with risk levels. What should be configured?
options: Sensitive Data Protection discovery profiles published to Security Command Center
questions.correct_rationale: Discovery profiles feed data risk into SCC.
questions.distractor_summary: Spreadsheets, CDN, and NAT logs do not show data risk.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: Users should see masked values in a sensitive BigQuery column unless they have a special role. What should be used?
options: BigQuery dynamic data masking with policy tags and data masking rules
Copy the table without the column for each user
Store the column in Cloud Storage

questions.distractor_summary: Deleting or copying data is wasteful, and moving to Storage does not mask.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss

options: Filters rows returned to users based on row access policies

questions.distractor_summary: It does not encrypt, delete, or compress.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: What is Secret Manager used for?
options: Storing, versioning, and controlling access to secrets such as API keys and passwords
questions.correct_rationale: Secret Manager securely stores secrets with IAM and audit logs.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not host containers, scan images, or route traffic.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: Secrets must rotate automatically every 30 days. What should be configured?
options: A rotation schedule on the secret that publishes to Pub/Sub, triggering a function that creates a new version
Store secrets in code with comments

questions.distractor_summary: Manual memory, code storage, and no rotation are unsafe.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss

options: Bucket retention policy, which can be locked

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: Cloud Storage access must be managed only through IAM, not object ACLs. What should be enabled?

questions.distractor_summary: Versioning, requester pays, and Autoclass do not disable ACLs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: What is a signed URL in Cloud Storage?
options: A URL that grants time-limited access to a specific object without requiring a Google account
questions.correct_rationale: Signed URLs give temporary, scoped access.
questions.distractor_summary: They are not permanent, DNS, or firewall rules.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: Data loss prevention scans of large BigQuery tables are costly. How can cost be reduced?
options: Scan every table hourly in full
Export all tables to CSV first
Use sampling, limit the rows scanned, and target the most relevant tables and columns
questions.correct_rationale: Sampling and targeting reduce scanned bytes.
questions.distractor_summary: Frequent full scans raise cost, exporting adds work, and logging is unrelated.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: What does the Sensitive Data Protection "risk analysis" feature measure?
options: Re-identification risk metrics such as k-anonymity and l-diversity for datasets
questions.correct_rationale: Risk analysis estimates how easily people can be re-identified.
questions.distractor_summary: It does not measure latency, CPU, or disks.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: A company wants to block uploads of files containing sensitive data in Google Workspace and Chrome. Which capability fits?
options: Data protection rules (DLP) for Workspace and Chrome Enterprise
questions.correct_rationale: Workspace and Chrome DLP rules inspect and block sensitive content.
questions.distractor_summary: Armor, firewalls, and load balancing do not inspect file contents.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss
questions.question: Which Data Catalog or Dataplex feature helps classify and tag data assets for governance?
options: Dataplex Universal Catalog with tags and aspects
questions.correct_rationale: Catalog metadata supports discovery and governance of data assets.
questions.distractor_summary: NAT, VPN, and VM metadata are not data catalogs.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: How is data at rest encrypted by default in Google Cloud?
options: Not at all unless customers enable it
Automatically with Google-managed encryption keys, with no customer action needed
questions.correct_rationale: Google encrypts all customer data at rest by default.
questions.distractor_summary: Encryption is automatic, covers services, and applies in all regions.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: A regulation requires that the company control and rotate the keys used to encrypt BigQuery data. What should be used?
options: Customer-supplied keys stored in a spreadsheet
Customer-managed encryption keys (CMEK) in Cloud KMS
questions.correct_rationale: CMEK lets customers manage key lifecycle in Cloud KMS.
questions.distractor_summary: Default keys are Google controlled, spreadsheets are not key storage, and no encryption breaks policy.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: What is the key hierarchy in Cloud KMS?
options: Key rings contain keys, and keys contain key versions
questions.correct_rationale: Key rings group keys in a location, and each key has versions.
questions.distractor_summary: The other structures are wrong.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: Keys must be stored in FIPS 140-2 Level 3 validated hardware. What protection level should be chosen?
options: HSM protection level in Cloud KMS (Cloud HSM)

questions.distractor_summary: Software keys are not HSM-backed, keys in code are unsafe, and protection level is required.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: What does Cloud External Key Manager (Cloud EKM) provide?
options: Using keys stored in a supported external key manager outside Google to protect data in Google Cloud

questions.distractor_summary: It does not store keys in buckets, encrypt VPNs, or rotate passwords.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: A key used for CMEK must rotate every 90 days automatically. What should be configured?
options: An automatic rotation period of 90 days on the Cloud KMS key
questions.correct_rationale: Automatic rotation creates new primary versions on schedule.
questions.distractor_summary: Manual reminders are unreliable, deletion destroys data access, and disabling breaks encryption.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: What happens to data encrypted with a CMEK key version when that version is destroyed?
options: The data is re-encrypted automatically with Google keys
The data becomes unrecoverable, because it cannot be decrypted
The data moves to another region
questions.correct_rationale: Destroying a key version makes data encrypted with it unreadable.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not re-encrypted automatically, there is impact, and data does not move.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: Protection against accidental key destruction is required. What safeguards should be used?
options: Keep the default scheduled-for-destruction period (or lengthen it), restrict destroy permissions, and consider a deny policy
Set the destruction period to zero
questions.correct_rationale: Scheduled destruction gives time to restore, and limited permissions reduce risk.
questions.distractor_summary: Broad admin rights and zero delay increase risk, and keys must not be in code.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: What is Cloud KMS Autokey?
options: A feature that creates CMEK keys automatically on demand when resources are created, following recommended practices

questions.distractor_summary: It is not a password manager, VPN, or firewall.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: Data in transit between Google data centers is a concern. What is true?
options: Google encrypts data in transit between its facilities, and applications should still use TLS
No traffic is ever encrypted in Google networks
Customers must buy a separate service for basic encryption in transit
Only Cloud Storage traffic is encrypted
questions.correct_rationale: Google applies encryption in transit across its network, and TLS protects end to end.
questions.distractor_summary: The other statements are incorrect.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: What does Confidential Computing protect?

questions.correct_rationale: Confidential VMs and GKE nodes keep memory encrypted during processing.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: What are customer-supplied encryption keys (CSEK)?

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: Certificates for internal services must be issued and managed privately. What should be used?
questions.correct_rationale: CA Service runs managed private CAs.
questions.distractor_summary: DNS, Armor, and NAT do not issue certificates.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: Which load balancer feature lets you control TLS versions and cipher suites for clients?
questions.correct_rationale: SSL policies set minimum TLS versions and cipher profiles.
questions.distractor_summary: Health checks, URL maps, and backend buckets do not control TLS.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
questions.question: CMEK must be used for all new resources in supported services across the organization. What enforces this?
options: The constraints/gcp.restrictNonCmekServices and gcp.restrictCmekCryptoKeyProjects organization policies
questions.correct_rationale: These constraints require CMEK and limit which key projects can be used.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use

options: Using one key for all data forever
Encrypting data with a data encryption key, then encrypting that key with a key encryption key
questions.correct_rationale: Envelope encryption is how Google and KMS protect data keys.
questions.distractor_summary: It is not physical, single-key forever, or no encryption.

questions.exam: Google Cloud Professional Cloud Security Engineer
questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss

questions.subdomain: 3.1 Protecting sensitive data and preventing data loss

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use

questions.subdomain: 3.2 Managing encryption at rest, in transit, and in use
